title: 981. Minimum Cost to Merge Stones

examples.explanation: Merge pairwise from the left: costs accumulate to 20.
Four piles cannot shrink to one by removing two piles per move.
First merge [5,1,2] at cost 8, then merge everything at cost 17.

hints: Merging to one pile is possible exactly when (n - 1) is divisible by (k - 1); otherwise return -1.
Use interval DP: dp[i][j] is the cheapest cost to shrink piles i..j, trying every split spaced k-1 apart.
Add the interval sum on top only when the interval can collapse fully, i.e. (length - 1) is divisible by (k - 1).
